justification.critique_assessment: The objections are valid and highlight plausible downward pressures (attribution uncertainty, deterrence, and non-battlefield CS evidence) that warrant a lower final probability.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.50 to 0.38 to reflect net downward pressures from attribution uncertainty and deterrence, while preserving upside risk from observed CS activity.

forecasts.reference-class: Probability that a state actor uses chemical weapons in a contemporary interstate armed conflict (modern warfare), i.e., a state-on-state confrontation under the Chemical Weapons Convention regime.

sources.claim: Key forecasts: Risk of use of chemical or biological weapons in the next 12 months: 12% (median forecast).
OPCW Technical Assistance Visit confirmed presence of the riot-control agent CS in Ukraine-related samples from the Sept 2024 Illinka incident.
OPCW findings of CS presence in alleged battlefield incidents; attribution not established.
OPCW annual reports document the Chemical Weapons Convention framework and ongoing monitoring related to Ukraine.
Dutch and German intelligence say Russia has stepped up use of banned chemical weapons in Ukraine (chloropicrin, CS); reports cite normalization concerns.
Kyiv/Ukraine claims OPCW reports show thousands of chemical-warfare incidents in Ukraine and confirmation of CS presence.
Risk of use of chemical or biological weapons in the next 12 months: 12%, with forecasters noting a range from about 1% to 23%.
OPCW findings show additional evidence of chemical weapons use in Ukraine (presence of CS in three October 2024 incidents), though attribution remains undetermined.
Dutch and German intelligence agencies allege Russia is expanding its use of chemical weapons in Ukraine, including chloropicrin.
OPCW confirms presence of the riot-control agent CS in three October 2024 incidents in Ukraine and notes that use of riot-control agents as a weapon is prohibited.
OPCW monitors chemical weapons-related incidents in Ukraine and provides technical assistance and capacity-building in response to ongoing concerns since 2022.
OPCW findings (Feb 2025) confirm CS in three separate incidents along Ukrainian front lines; attribution of responsibility remains unsettled.
Dutch and German intelligence report that Russia has stepped up use of banned chemical weapons in Ukraine, including chloropicrin and CS, describing such use as increasingly standardised.
France welcomes the OPCW report confirming use of riot-control agents and reiterates condemnation of their use as a method of warfare.

synthesis: The objections identify genuine blind spots in attribution and deterrence, justifying a downward tilt from the ensemble. Nevertheless, verified CS-related activity and credible intelligence keep a nonzero risk through May 1, 2026, supporting a tempered, central estimate around 0.38.
